verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तथैव राजा कौन्तेयो धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखान् वीरांश्चोदयामास भारत ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said In the same way the virtuous king Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, urged the warriors headed by Dhrishtadyumna, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: चेदिकाशिकरूषाणां नेतारं दृढविक्रमम्। सेनापतिममित्रघ्नं धृष्टकेतुमथादिशत् ॥२॥
verses.english: He ordered the leaders and commander of the Chedis, Kashis, and Karushas, Dhrishtaketu, of steady prowess, and the slayer of foes,

verses.sanskrit: विराटं द्रुपदं चैव युयुधानं शिखण्डिनम्। पाञ्चाल्यौ च महेष्वासौ युधामन्यूत्तमौजसौ॥३॥
verses.english: And Virata, and Drupada and Yuyudhana and Shikhandin, and the mighty archers, rulers of Panchalas, the two Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas (to advance).

verses.sanskrit: ते शूराश्चित्रवर्माणस्तप्तकुण्डलधारिणः। आज्यावसिक्ता ज्वलिता धिष्ण्येष्विव हुताशनाः ॥४॥
verses.english: Those warriors, clad in variegated armours, and bearing golden ear-rings shone like clarified butter is poured (or them).

verses.sanskrit: अशोभन्त महेष्वासा ग्रहाः प्रज्वलिता इव। अथ सैन्यं यथायोगं पूजयित्वा नरर्षभः ॥५॥
verses.english: Those mighty archers shone beautiful like burning constellations. At length having paid due homage to the army, that best among men,

verses.sanskrit: दिदेश तान्यनीकानि प्रयाणाय महीपतिः। तेषां युधिष्ठिरो राजा ससैन्यानां महात्मनाम् ॥६॥
verses.english: The ruler of the earth, ordered those forces to advance. And king Yudhishthira ordered for those high-souled (warriors) with forces, consisting of infantry.

verses.sanskrit: व्यादिदेश सबाह्यानां भक्ष्यभोज्यमनुत्तमम्। सगजाश्वमनुष्याणां ये च शिल्पोपजीविनः ॥७॥
verses.english: Together with elephants and steeds and other followers, provisions of the best kind, as well as for those who lived by means of mechanical arts.

verses.sanskrit: अभिमन्युं बृहन्तं च द्रौपदेयांश्च सर्वशः। घृष्टद्युम्नमुखानेतान् प्राहिणोत् पाण्डुनन्दनः ॥८॥
verses.english: And the son of Pandu ordered Abhimanyu and Brihanta and all Draupadeyas, (the five sons of Draupadi), headed by Dhrishtadyumna, to advance.

verses.sanskrit: भीमं च युयुधानं च पाण्डवं च धनञ्जयम्। द्वितीयं प्रेषयामास बलस्कन्धं युधिष्ठिरः ॥९॥
verses.english: And then he sent forth the second division of the army with Bhima, Yuyudhana and Dhananjaya, the son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: भाण्डं समारोपयतां चरतां संप्रधावताम्। हृष्टानां तत्र योधानां शब्दो दिवमिवास्पृशत् ॥१०॥
verses.english: And the noise of the warriors as they put on the equipment's of war, and moved and ran about, cheered as they were, reached the very heavens.

verses.sanskrit: स्वयमेव ततः पश्चाद्विराटद्रुपदान्वितः। अथापरैर्महीपालैः सह प्रायान्महीपतिः ॥११॥
verses.english: Last of all, that ruler of the earth himself went forth in the rear, with other rulers of the earth, accompanied by Virata and Drupada.

verses.sanskrit: भीमधन्वायनी सेना धृष्टद्युम्नेन पालिता। गङ्गेव पूर्णा स्तिमिता स्यन्दमाना व्यदृश्यत ॥१२॥
verses.english: Then that army, of terrible archers commanded by Dhrishtadyumna, as it moved to and fro, looked like the full Ganga, silently rushing on.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पुनरनीकानि न्ययोजयत बुद्धिमान्। मोहयन् धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणां बुद्धिनिश्चयम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then the intelligent (Yudhishthira) again arranged his troops (in a different order), confounding the knowledge of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदेयान्महेष्वासानभिमन्युं च पाण्डवः। नकुलं सहदेवं च सर्वांश्चैव प्रभद्रकान् ॥१४॥
verses.english: And the son of Pandu ordered the five sons of Draupadi who were mighty bowmen, and Abhimanyu Nakula and Sahadeva, and all the Prabhadraka, and ten thousand horses and elephants; and ten thousand foot-soldiers, and five hundred chariots, to be the first division of the ariny, under the irresistible Bhimasena. And the son of Pandu (ordered) in the middle (division of his army) Virata and Jayatsena,

verses.sanskrit: दश चाश्वसहस्राणि द्विसहस्त्राणि दन्तिनाम्। अयुतं च पदातीनां रथाः पञ्चशतं तथा ॥१५॥
भीमसेनस्य दुर्धर्षं प्रथमं प्रादिशद्बलम्। मध्यमे च विराटं च जयत्सेनं च पाण्डवः ॥१६॥
महारथौ च पाञ्चाल्यौ युधामन्यूत्तमौजसौ। वीर्यवन्तौ महात्मानौ गदाकार्मुकधारिणौ ॥१७॥
verses.english: And the two Maharathas, the ruler of Panchala, Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas, who were high-souled (warriors) of great prowess holding clubs and bows.

verses.sanskrit: अन्वयातां तदा मध्ये वासुदेवधनञ्जयौ। बभूवुरतिसंरब्धाः कृतप्रहरणा नराः ॥१८॥
verses.english: And in this middle division followed Vasudeva and Dhananjaya. And these were men well-accomplished in arms, burning with anger.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां विंशतिसाहस्रा हयाः शूरैरधिष्ठिताः। पञ्च नागसहस्त्राणि रथवंशाश्च सर्वशः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Amongst them were twenty thousand horses ridden by brave warriors, and five thousand elephants and cars on all sides round.

verses.sanskrit: पदायतश्च ये शूराः कार्मुकासिगदाधराः। सहस्रशोऽन्वयुः पश्चादग्रतश्च सहस्रशः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Those warriors who composed the infantry, armed with bows, swords, and maces, followed by thousands in the vanguard, and thousands in the rear.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरो यत्र सैन्ये स्वयमेव बलार्णवे। तत्र ते पृथिवीपाला भूयिष्ठं पर्यवस्थिताः ॥२१॥
verses.english: And in that part of that ocean of forces, where Yudhishthira himself (was), stationed a large number of rulers of the earth.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र नागसहस्राणि हयानामयुतानि च। तथा रथसहस्त्राणि पदातीनां च भारत ॥२२॥
verses.english: And in that part (were) thousands of elephants, and ten thousands of steeds, as well as thousands of cars and foot-soldiers O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: चेकितानः स्वसैन्येन महता पार्थिवर्षभ। धृष्टकेतुश्च चेदीनां प्रणेता पार्थिवो ययौ ॥२३॥
verses.english: And Chekitana, with his own mighty force, O best among kings, and king Dhrishtaketu, the leader of the Chedis, marched forth.

verses.sanskrit: सात्यकिश्च महेष्वासो वृष्णीनां प्रवरो रथः। वृतः शतसहस्त्रेण रथानां प्रणुदन् बली ॥२४॥
verses.english: And there (was) also Satyaki, that archer and the best of the car-warriors among the Vrishnis, surrounded by hundreds and thousands of chariots, and leading (them) forward, powerful as he was.

verses.sanskrit: क्षत्रदेवब्रह्मदेवौ रथस्थौ पुरुषर्षभौ। जघनं पालयन्तौ च पृष्ठतोऽनुप्रजग्मतुः ॥२५॥
verses.english: And those foremost among men, seated on their chariots, Kshatradeva and Brahmadeva, followed behind, protecting the rear.

verses.sanskrit: शकटापणवेशाश्च यानं युग्यं च सर्वशः। तत्र नागसहस्राणि हयानामयुतानि च। फल्गु सर्वं कलत्रं च यत्किञ्चित् कृशदुर्बलम् ॥२६॥
verses.english: And there were (in the rear) carts shops, vehicles, and beast of burden of all kinds and thousands of elephants and ten thousands of steeds. And all the children and women, and those who were emaciated and weak.

verses.sanskrit: कोशसञ्चयवाहांश्च कोष्ठागारं तथैव च। गजानीकेन संगृह्य शनैः प्रायाद्युधिष्ठिरः ॥२७॥
verses.english: And with the animals carrying his treasures, and his granaries and uniting all these by means of an army of elephants, king Yudhishthira slowly marched forward.
verses.bhavadeepa: शकटा भाण्डवन्ति अनांसि । आपणो वणिक्समुदायः वेशो वेश्याजनः यानं युद्धयोग्यं वाहनं युग्यं केवलं वाहनं फल्गु बालादिकम् । कलत्रं स्त्र्यादिकम् ॥२६॥

verses.sanskrit: तमन्वयात् सत्यधृतिः सौचित्तिर्युद्धदुर्मदः। श्रेणिमान् वसुदानश्च पुत्रः काश्यस्य वा विभुः॥२८॥
verses.english: Him (Yudhishthira) followed Suchitta, an unswerving adherent of truth, and who was invincible in battle, and Shrenimat and Vasudeva, and Vibhu, the son of the Kashis.
verses.bhavadeepa: कोशो धनं कोष्ठो धान्यादिसामग्री सङ्गृह्य एकीकृत्य ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: रथा विंशतिसाहस्रा ये तेषामनुयायिनः। हयानां दश कोट्यश्च महतां किंकिणीकिनाम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: And they followed him, with twenty thousand chariots, and a hundred million steeds (of that mighty army) with great bells,

verses.sanskrit: गजा विंशतिसाहस्रा ईषादन्ताः प्रहारिणः। कुलीना भिन्नकरटा मेघा इव विसर्पिणः ॥३०॥
verses.english: And twenty thousand elephants who smote with their tusks resembling plowshares all of good breed, and with spit temples and moving about like masses of clouds.

verses.sanskrit: षष्ठिर्नागसहस्त्राणि दशान्यानि च भारत। युधिष्ठिरस्य यान्यासन् युधि सेना महात्मनः ॥३१॥
verses.english: And besides these, O Bharata, thousand elephants which were in the seven divisions of the army of Yudhishthira in that battle,

verses.sanskrit: क्षरन्त इव जीमूताः प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः। राजानमन्वयुः पश्चाच्चलन्त इव पर्वताः ॥३२॥
verses.english: With temporal juice flowing down and with the temples rent, followed the king like so many moving mountains.

verses.sanskrit: एवं तस्य बलं भीमं कुन्तीपुत्रस्य धीमतः। यदाश्रित्याथ युयुधे धार्तराष्ट्रं सुयोधनम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Such was the terrible array of forces of that wise son of Kunti, relying on the help of which he fought with Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽन्ये शतशः पश्चात् सहस्त्रायुतशो नराः। नर्दन्तः प्रययुस्तेषामनीकानि सहस्रशः ॥३४॥
verses.english: And above these, other men, by hundreds and thousands and tens of thousands of groups o thousands, followed their (sons of Pandu) forces, roaring loudly.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र भेरीसहस्राणि शङ्खानामयुतानि च। न्यवादयन्त संहृष्टाः सहस्त्रायुतशो नराः ॥३५॥
verses.english: And those men by thousands and tens of thousand, filled with joy, beat their drums by thousands, and blew their conches by tens of thousands.
